not_covered: This corpus is checked statically: each case's facts lead to its route by the decision order, each decided_by quotes a clause of _shared/flow-applicability.md, and every clause is cited. It does not prove that a model, given a real request, answers the four facts correctly; to measure that, run the requests by hand against a real model and compare the facts, outside the suite.

cases.request: Why does this project use SDD at all, when most of it was built with a single architecture file for progress and decisions?
cases.decided_by: `output_is_information` → **query**.

cases.request: Walk me through how past features were tracked in one architecture file instead of SDD, and whether that should shape a lighter lane.
cases.decided_by: **Query** when the output ends the work: explain, compare, investigate, audit, review, run a check, or propose without authorization to implement. It changes nothing.

cases.request: Check whether the status recorded for the pending release is still true, without changing anything.
cases.decided_by: **Query** when the output ends the work: explain, compare, investigate, audit, review, run a check, or propose without authorization to implement. It changes nothing.

cases.request: Does a candidate dependency really lack a published download URL, or did we only assume it?
cases.decided_by: `output_is_information` → **query**.

cases.request: Do the two open upstream issues blocking a permission fix show any sign of being fixed?
cases.decided_by: `output_is_information` → **query**.

cases.request: Did the install failure someone reported really come from a bad checksum, or from something else?
cases.decided_by: `output_is_information` → **query**.

cases.request: Audit every module of the core for imports that reach into an adapter and report what you find; change nothing.
cases.decided_by: **Query** when the output ends the work: explain, compare, investigate, audit, review, run a check, or propose without authorization to implement. It changes nothing.

cases.request: Find out why the test suite got slow and tell me what you would change; do not touch anything yet.
cases.decided_by: **Query** when the output ends the work: explain, compare, investigate, audit, review, run a check, or propose without authorization to implement. It changes nothing.

cases.request: Fix the error message so the real failure reason is no longer hidden behind a long URL.
cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.request: Stop a core error formatter from depending on text that only an adapter promises to add.
cases.decided_by: **L0** when the change is one trivial, atomic, known intervention with no decision to settle, provable with one proportionate piece of evidence. It leaves a diff, that evidence and an honest report, and no record.

cases.request: A test leaves a stale cached attribute behind for the next test; fix its teardown.
cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.request: A preflight check treats 'not installed' and 'installed but will not start' as the same case; split them.
cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.decided_by: **L0** when the change is one trivial, atomic, known intervention with no decision to settle, provable with one proportionate piece of evidence. It leaves a diff, that evidence and an honest report, and no record.

cases.request: The release goes out tonight: stop the installer from aborting silently under strict shell flags when a version string spans two lines.
cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.request: `upgrade` treats any different version as newer, so an older release silently downgrades the binary; compare versions properly.
cases.decided_by: None of the above → **L0**.

cases.request: A shipped adapter file hardcodes the orchestrator's name instead of reading it from content.
cases.decided_by: **L0** when the change is one trivial, atomic, known intervention with no decision to settle, provable with one proportionate piece of evidence. It leaves a diff, that evidence and an honest report, and no record.

cases.request: A safety guard only worked because a hardcoded literal matched our own name; find out why it passed and derive the name from the identity file.
cases.decided_by: **A bug fix with an unclear cause.** Investigate before routing; once the cause is confirmed, the fix routes by its own facts.

cases.request: Update the year in the license header of every source file.
cases.decided_by: **One trivial operation across many files** stays **L0**.

cases.request: Instrument the test suite over several passes to find what really makes it slow, and fix the worst offender.
cases.decided_by: `needs_continuity` → **FTD**.

cases.request: Publish a release end to end and write up, with evidence, which fixes came from user reports and which from audits.
cases.decided_by: **FTD** when the change is decided enough to apply, needs no reviewable contract, and does need continuity, a checklist, durable evidence or a handoff. Ask until the scope is closed, then confirm once before writing.

cases.request: Decide how the filesystem layer tells a missing path apart from an unreadable one across a dozen call sites, then apply it.
cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.request: Replace a content-hash permission model with explicit snapshot and restore, deciding the retention count along the way.
cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.request: Decide whether the per-platform installers share one script with their differences applied at build time, or each keep a full copy of it.
cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.request: Decide what a routing fact means, how many clarifying questions an agent may ask, and whether a verifier may ever issue a readiness verdict.
cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.request: Bump the dependency to its next major version and fix whatever it breaks.
cases.decided_by: **Large but already decided.** A dependency upgrade with known fallout, a mechanical migration, a cross-cutting rename or a refactor whose behaviour the tests already state is **FTD** however many files it touches.

cases.request: Finish the adapter cleanup over the next few sessions, leaving a checklist the next session can pick up.
cases.decided_by: **Work that crosses sessions or leaves a record behind.** A checklist the next session picks up, or a record that outlives the session, is continuity: **FTD**.

cases.request: The upgrade check fails on some machines; the cause is confirmed in how three modules compare versions, and each needs its own fix and evidence.
cases.decided_by: **A bug fix with an unclear cause.** Investigate before routing; once the cause is confirmed, the fix routes by its own facts.

cases.request: Two reasonable designs for the cache came up during the migration; pick one with me, write down why, and carry on.
cases.decided_by: **A decision or a trade-off to settle.** On its own it is not SDD: decide it with the person, write it down with the work, and go on as **FTD**.

cases.request: Open an SDD change to replace the clean-install foundation with an additive engine that never deletes a user's existing setup.
cases.decided_by: `asked_for_sdd` → **SDD**; the explicit request is the acceptance.

cases.request: Write a spec for the release-acceptance contract and an agent-safe preflight that other release tooling will build against.
cases.decided_by: `asked_for_sdd` → **SDD**; the explicit request is the acceptance.

cases.request: Add one optional field to the journal format that two other tools read without being part of this change.
cases.decided_by: **A small change to a contract others build against.** Two lines can still need a spec: when consumers outside the change build against them, it is **SDD**.

cases.request: Define the interface third-party adapters will implement, before any of them is written.
cases.decided_by: **SDD** when someone absent from the implementation must review a contract or a decision before code; when others build against its spec, API, authorization or data model; when others will execute its ordered units; or when it was asked for.

cases.request: Change the exit code `doctor` returns on drift; scripts written by people outside this change branch on it.
cases.decided_by: `needs_reviewable_contract` → **SDD** is proposed, and entered only on explicit acceptance.

cases.request: Split the content-format migration into ordered units that other contributors will implement without us.
cases.decided_by: `needs_reviewable_contract` → **SDD** is proposed, and entered only on explicit acceptance.

cases.request: Investigate why the release build got slow; the findings leave a fix that spans several passes, each with its own measurement, and the person says to go ahead.
cases.decided_by: **Query → L0, FTD or SDD** when the investigation leaves an executable proposal. A query authorizes no change: ask once whether to go ahead, and the investigation becomes the new route's input.

cases.request: Backport a generic fix to the maintenance branch; once the same two failures recur on every backport, turn the ritual into a written, numbered procedure.
cases.decided_by: **L0 → FTD** when the change stops being atomic: several tasks, another session or a handoff, grouped evidence, more surface than planned, or a decision worth recording. Carry over what was done as it really happened, never as if FTD had been there from the start.

cases.request: Rename a field in the `doctor` report; midway it turns out tools outside this change parse that report.
cases.decided_by: **L0 → SDD** when a `needs_reviewable_contract` appears. A decision taken and landed in the same work promotes to FTD instead.

cases.request: Midway through a multi-module refactor, the change reaches the interface that third-party adapters implement.
cases.decided_by: **FTD → SDD** when a `needs_reviewable_contract` appears or SDD, a spec or a plan is asked for. Two reasonable designs or a trade-off, on their own, do not promote: they are decided, written down, and the FTD goes on.
